_what_this_is: Section P's conditions are measured over every archived panel reply. When a
round falls short of one, the shortfall is RECORDED HERE WITH ITS MEASURED
CAUSE rather than excused, and the guards assert that nothing NEW joins this
list. That is the convention the guards already used for
panel_roster_fix_2026-09-09, which was dispatched before the disagreement
WHY A RECORD AND NOT AN EXEMPTION. A shortfall that is deleted from the
archive, or silently dropped from a population, stops being evidence. Every
entry below is a round that really did fall short, with the defect that
caused it and the commit that fixed it, so the record answers 'why' rather
RULES FOR EDITING. Name the round and the seat exactly. State the CAUSE as a
measurement, not an impression. State whether it is fixed, and name the test
that holds the fix. A new entry is a claim that something went wrong and was
understood -- never a way to make a red suite green.

shortfalls.what: The seat recorded 0 tool calls and returned 0 characters.
cause: The Kimi seat was dispatched through call_moonshot into the shared tool
loop, whose default_tool_executor knew only the name `execute_python`.
Every tool the brief offered came back to the seat as `[unknown tool]`,
so the harness was not available to be used. P3 asks whether the seat
USED the harness; on this round there was no harness to use.
shortfalls.fix: default_tool_executor now routes unknown names to dispatch_tool_call, so the access tools reach the executor that implements them (bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.py).

shortfalls.what: 0 characters returned after 1 tool call that read 24,868 characters.
cause: bench/openrouter_tools.py treated empty visible content as a finished
answer: on a turn with no tool calls it took `msg.content or ''`, set
stopped_reason='finish' and broke. Its sibling loop in
experiment_11_orchestrator.py has carried a tool-less retry at a raised
budget for exactly this case since 2026-06-06, written against
gemini-3.1-pro-preview. The loop the paid seats actually run never
received it, so the very model the retry was written for hit the very
failure it prevents.
shortfalls.fix: The retry is now in the paid-seat loop, and a reply that stays empty is recorded as 'empty_content_after_retry' rather than 'finish'.

shortfalls.what: 0 characters returned after 25 successful tool calls over 216 seconds.
cause: The forced-synthesis call in _run_openai_tool_loop hardcoded
temperature=0.0 while the loop's own `temperature` parameter -- added the
same day for kimi-k3, which refuses any value but 1 -- was threaded only
into the main request. Every retry raised HTTP 400 and a bare `except`
swallowed it, discarding 25 tool calls of real work.
shortfalls.fix: The forced-synthesis call now uses the caller's temperature.

shortfalls.what: The reply carried no disagreement because it carried nothing at all: 0 characters, ok=False, after 29 SUCCESSFUL tool calls over 1116.8 seconds. The other 6 seats of this round all carried a disagreement, so the round was not smoothed to consensus; 1 seat died.
cause: NOT DETERMINED FROM THE RECORD, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE DEFECT. The seat's
last tool call succeeded and returned real analysis -- it had just computed
expected_binary_review(1/2, 4/5, 0, (1,0), (0,0)) = 1/10 against the revised
specification -- so the work was in flight and the final synthesis returned
nothing.
Why the cause cannot be recovered: in bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py
`stopped_reason` and `tool_iterations` are assigned ONLY in the openrouter
branch. The moonshot and deepseek branch never assigns them, and the record
is built with `locals().get('stopped_reason')`, so those fields are None BY
CONSTRUCTION on this route rather than because nothing went wrong. The
1116.8s elapsed is well inside the route's 1500s timeout, so it was not a
timeout, and `attempts` is empty, so no retry was recorded either.
This is NOT a recurrence of the 2026-09-20_r3 kimi defect. That one was the
forced-synthesis call hardcoding temperature=0.0 against a model that
refuses any value but 1, and it is fixed; `call_moonshot` drives
`_run_openai_tool_loop`, so that fix does reach this route. Nor is it the
P3 entry's cause: tools were available here and 29 of them ran.
It is the same SHAPE as the 2026-09-20_r3 `ge` entry -- a diagnostic that
exists on one sibling path and not on the one the paid seat actually runs.
shortfalls.fix: OUTSTANDING. The actionable item is the instrumentation, not a guess at the failure: the moonshot and deepseek branch must record a stopped_reason so that a 0-character paid reply is diagnosable at all. Deliberately not attempted on 2026-09-21, because validating a change to a paid dispatch path requires a paid dispatch, and the founder was asleep. It does not block the commissioning study, which is simulated and spends nothing.

shortfalls.what: The reply carries no disagreement FIELD. The SUBSTANCE was present and the word was not: it refuted the brief's own declared figure, recording that "the brief's '73 of 73' is a hardcoded literal in the figures script, not a live count; the live deduplicated count is 201". The project accepted that refutation and WITHDREW the figure. So the round was not smoothed to consensus by this seat; it dissented and filed the dissent under the heading "Two corrections I owe".
cause: MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. The reply is 4235 characters, ok=True, after 157
tool calls, and it ends with its own stopping statement -- "Stopped on
diminishing returns at pass 5" -- so it is complete and was not truncated.
A token census over the whole reply returns 0 occurrences of each of
disagree, disagreement, dissent and diverge.
THE BRIEF ASKED TWICE, so instruction was not the gap:
bench/logs/a19_calculator_design_2026-09-30/BRIEF.md line 14 ("If you
disagree with the other seat, say so and say why, with evidence") and line
78 ("Name any disagreement with the other seat explicitly").
AND THE BRIEF ASKED FOR SOMETHING THIS ROUND'S DESIGN CANNOT SUPPLY. Both
seats answer the same brief in parallel, in separate sandboxes, with no
sight of each other's reply, so no seat can disagree with THE OTHER SEAT's
content. The only objects available are CC1 and the brief, and this seat
disagreed with the brief.
WHY THE GUARD COULD NOT SEE IT. DISAGREEMENT_RE matches the WORD. A
refutation written as a correction is invisible to it, and no lexical
widening can close that gap without matching mentions as well as
assertions -- the defect that would weaken the guard in the reassuring
direction. The widening applied the same day was the part that CAN be done
safely: it recovered 4 replies, including this round's OTHER seat, which
named its disagreement with CC1 inside a question heading. 0 replies were
lost, measured over all 306 archived seat replies.
THE OTHER SEAT OF THIS ROUND PRESERVED ITS DISAGREEMENT, so P5's actual
subject -- that disagreement survives into the record rather than being
smoothed -- holds for the round.
shortfalls.fix: OUTSTANDING AND IT IS THE FOUNDER'S TO SETTLE, because the options change his `pr` protocol rather than any code. (1) Require the field as a NAMED SECTION in the brief, which makes compliance mechanically checkable at the cost of prescribing form. (2) Name the object correctly for a blind parallel round -- disagreement with CC1 or with the brief, since the other seat's reply is unreadable by design. (3) Leave it, on the ground that a seat which refutes the brief's own figure has done the thing the condition exists to protect. No code change is proposed here: the round is archived and cannot be re-run, and widening the guard further would make it match mentions. Recorded 2026-10-01T14:10:24+01:00.

shortfalls.what: The seat stated no disagreement in the STAR round, having stated one in the blind round.
cause: Measured by executing the extractor over both rounds: blind round cc2 True,
fable True; star round cc2 True, fable False. The blind brief made
'STRONGEST DISAGREEMENT WITH THIS BRIEF'S OWN FRAMING -- mandatory' an
OUTPUT FIELD at line 69. The star brief's REQUIRED SECTION 5 replaced that
output shape with RESOLUTION / WHO WAS RIGHT / EVIDENCE / FIX / WHAT WOULD
REFUTE THIS / CONFIDENCE and dropped the field, asking for disagreement
only as prose in the termination section. The single occurrence of the
phrase in the star brief is at line 456, inside fable's own embedded
round-1 reply -- so the brief asked for it nowhere in its own body.
The defect is the BRIEF's, not the seat's: a star round's purpose is to
reconcile, which makes it the round most able to produce agreement by
deference, and the one brief that most needed the field is the one that
lost it.
shortfalls.fix: panel_brief_validate.py now refuses a brief whose OUTPUT SECTION does not name disagreement as a field (scripts/panel_brief_validate.py). What justifies it is TEMPLATE CONFORMANCE: panel_brief_template.md's output section already asks for 'the strongest disagreement with the brief's own framing' by name and passes the check unchanged, so the defect was a validator permitting divergence from the standard it enforces -- 12 of 95 archived briefs diverged and nothing caught them. The check is SECTION SCOPED because a document-wide regex is defeated by the embedded previous-round replies a star brief carries: the word appears on 7 lines of the defective brief, so a document-wide check PASSES it. Measured over all 95 archived briefs, section scope refuses 12 (12.6316%, Wilson [7.3757%, 20.7921%]) and whole-document 15 (15.7895%, Wilson [9.8085%, 24.4296%]). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: that naming the field changes what seats return. Over 50 rounds carrying both a brief and replies, 32 of 38 with the field had every seat state a disagreement against 9 of 12 without it, Fisher exact two-sided p = 6.675478e-01 (within-period p = 6.187658e-01), scipy and mpmath agreeing to 1e-9. This entry's first version cited 2 figures, 82.1053% and '1 of 3', and both were false -- measured on 3 briefs read by hand rather than on the archive. Producer: scripts/brief_disagreement_field_effect_2026-10-02.py.

shortfalls.what: The seat recorded 0 tool calls and returned 0 characters after 3628.5 seconds.
cause: NOT A HARNESS DEFECT AND NOT THE SEAT DECLINING TO USE IT: the Claude CLI
call timed out. The reply records ok=False with
error='RuntimeError: Claude CLI call failed after 2 attempts for opus. Last
error: claude CLI timed out after 1800.1s', 3628.5 s of wall clock for 2
attempts at the 1800 s ceiling, 0 tool calls and 0 characters.
0 TOOL CALLS IN 1800 SECONDS, TWICE, IS THE DISTINGUISHING MEASUREMENT. A
seat that discussed the harness instead of using it would still have
produced text; a seat working and running out of clock would have produced
tool calls. This one produced neither, so the route never carried the
request. P3 asks whether the seat USED the harness; on this round the seat
never started.
THE SAME SHAPE RECURRED ON 2026-10-06 AND WAS MEASURED MORE FULLY. There,
cc2 timed out at 1800 s twice during reported network outages, the second
time having made 88 tool calls, and then answered the IDENTICAL brief in
1020.0 s with 49 tool calls once the link was stable. The per-call rate was
20.455 and 20.816 seconds across all 3 attempts, so the seat was never
slowed; only the call count moved. A degraded route therefore produces
either 0 calls or an inflated count, and in both cases 0 characters.
shortfalls.fix: FIXED BY PREVENTION RATHER THAN BY PATCHING THIS ROUND, which is archived and cannot be re-run. bench/seat_aliveness_2026-10-06.py asks every seat to print Ready! before any brief is sent, up to 3 attempts, and the dispatcher REFUSES the round when a seat does not answer. Measured live on 2026-10-06: the probe established a working route in 5.91 seconds, against the 3258 seconds a failed round took to establish the same fact. A route that cannot carry a request can therefore no longer produce a 0-tool-call reply that looks like a seat which did not use the harness. A dead seat refuses the whole round and is never dropped from the roster, because skipping a model is benching it.

shortfalls.what: The reply carried no disagreement because it carried nothing at all: 0 characters, ok=False, after 37 tool calls over 1956.0 seconds.
cause: A SHARED CAUSE, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOWS IT IS THE MATCHED CLOCK. Both
free seats failed on this round with ok=False and 0 characters at 1956.0 and
1956.2 seconds of elapsed time -- 0.2 seconds apart in 2 separate processes.
They did different amounts of work first: cc2 made 37 tool calls and fable
11. Independent failures do not land 0.2 seconds apart after unequal work;
only a cause outside both processes does.
Both seats authenticate against the SAME Max subscription, and until
2026-10-05 the dispatcher submitted them to a pool sized to the whole roster,
so both hit the CLI in the same instant. That is the contention hypothesis
already recorded in bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py, and this round is
its cleanest archived instance.
WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the record should not overstate it. Serialising
the free seats has NOT been shown to cure this: on 2026-10-06 the cc2 seat
ran alone, hours after fable had finished, and still failed twice -- though
that night also had reported network outages, so it is not a clean test
either. Contention explains the matched times here; it is not thereby proven
to be the only cause of an empty free-seat reply.
shortfalls.fix: PARTIALLY FIXED, AND THE REMAINDER IS NAMED. The free seats are serialised among themselves since 2026-10-05, so they no longer hit the subscription in the same instant. Independently, the 2026-10-06 aliveness probe refuses a round whose route does not answer, and scripts/panel_round_watchdog_2026-10-06.py re-dispatches a free round until a non-empty reply lands, refusing outright to dispatch any paid seat. What is NOT demonstrated is that serialisation cures the empty reply; that measurement needs a panel run both ways and is in the study programme.

shortfalls.what: The reply is not recognised as carrying a disagreement although it disagreed substantively: 4194 words, HOLDING against the other position's derivation on the minimum sample, with a quantified refutation. The round is the opposite of smoothed to consensus: the 2 seats CROSSED positions.
cause: THE OPERATOR'S BRIEF RENAMED THE FIELD, and the defect is a producer and a
consumer disagreeing about the same field while each is individually correct.
The joint brief asked for `## Residual disagreement`. `carries_disagreement`
in scripts/panel_condition_compliance_2026-09-10.py matches a heading whose
alternative requires the word to OPEN the line, so a qualifier in front of it
is invisible. Measured by calling the detector on both replies: False and
False, while a plain token search finds disagree, disagreement and Residual
in each.
AND THE BRIEF VALIDATOR PASSED IT, which is the real finding. It tested
`re.search(r'\\bdisagree', body)` -- a loose word search that `## Residual
disagreement` satisfies. So the validator's predicate was WEAKER than the
detector's, and a brief could declare a disagreement field that nothing would
ever recognise. This is the same SHAPE as the recorded
integrity_advisory_r2_2026-10-02 entry, where a star brief dropped the field
from its output shape; that entry's fix added the validator check, and this
one shows the check was too loose to close the gap it was built for.
shortfalls.fix: scripts/panel_brief_validate.py now holds the brief to the detector's OWN definition, importing DISAGREEMENT_RE from panel_condition_compliance_2026-09-10.py rather than restating the pattern, so a brief whose declared field the detector cannot read is REFUSED with a message naming the qualifier problem. Verified both ways by execution: the joint brief is now refused, and bench/directives/universal/panel_brief_template.md still passes all 8 required sections. The detector was deliberately NOT widened, because the 2026-10-02 entry records that widening makes it match mentions as well as assertions.
